title: How is Adolf Hitler connected to Thomas the Tank Engine?
description: Five real photos connect Adolf Hitler to Thomas the Tank Engine, through Finland's wartime marshal, a future Finnish president, a British prime minister and a Beatle.
hook: How is Adolf Hitler connected to Thomas the Tank Engine?
fun_fact: During Hitler's 1942 visit, a Finnish radio sound engineer secretly recorded the first 11 minutes of his talk with Mannerheim, the only known recording of Hitler speaking in an unofficial, everyday voice.
research_note: Instead of the usual Chamberlain or Franco exit, this chain leaves Hitler through Finland: the Finnish Heritage Agency's press archive has Mannerheim beside Kekkonen at a 1945 athletics match and Kekkonen with Harold Wilson at the 1975 Helsinki summit, and Wilson had handed the Beatles an award in 1964.

links.line: In 1942, Hitler flew to Finland for the 75th birthday of its wartime commander, Marshal Mannerheim.

image.credit: Otavamedia / JOKA press archive, Finnish Heritage Agency (Museovirasto)

links.line: In 1945, President Mannerheim watched athletics in Helsinki beside Urho Kekkonen, a future president of Finland.

image.credit: Atte Matilainen / JOKA press archive, Finnish Heritage Agency (Museovirasto)

links.line: In 1975, President Kekkonen hosted British prime minister Harold Wilson at the Helsinki summit.

image.credit: Terry O'Neill / Iconic Images (via Tristan's Gallery)

links.line: In 1964, Labour leader Harold Wilson handed Ringo Starr and the Beatles a showbiz award in London.

image.credit: Thomas the Tank Engine & Friends publicity photo (via Thomas & Friends Wiki)

links.line: And in 1984, Ringo Starr became the first TV voice of Thomas the Tank Engine.
